newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq plans to pump 6 mln bpd in 5-6 years time.
newsitem.headline: Iraq plans to pump 6 mln bpd in 5-6 years time.

text.p: Iraq plans to expand its oil export capacity to six million barrels per day (bpd) in five or six years, the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya quoted a senior oil official as saying on Wednesday.
"...The oil ministry is planning now and in the future to produce six million barrels per day (bpd) in five to six year time," said oil ministry undersecretary Fa'iz Abdullah Shahin.

He said Iraq had strategic plans with some countries to achieve such a production level. He said world oil consumption would increase in the year 2005 to 85 million bpd and the world would need eight million bpd of Iraq's oil.
He said Iraq's proven oil reserves were 112 billion barrels and its probable reserves were 214 billion barrels.

Baghdad has been negotiating with French and Russian firms to develop oilfields in the north and south of the country. A Russian delegation headed by Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov is currently in Iraq holding talks to conclude oil deals.
Iraq says its oil exports can be raised to that level once sanctions are lifted.
The United Nations embargo imposed on Iraq for invading Kuwait in 1990 bars trade with Baghdad.
The embargo includes a ban on oil exports but the U.N. has allowed Iraq to pump $2 billion worth of oil in six months to international markets on humanitarian grounds.
